profile.campus: Northwest Omaha, Douglas County, Nebraska (Google's newer Omaha campus, announced 2022, 261 acres near State Street and Blair High Road)
profile.address: State Street, Union Precinct, Douglas County, Nebraska, 68007
profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's northwest Omaha data center campus in Douglas County, announced in April 2022 as part of a $750 million Nebraska investment that year, itself part of a larger $9.5 billion national expansion Google announced across US data center and office sites. Google described the northwest Omaha project as a new multi-building campus on 261 acres near State Street and Blair High Road, matching this building's State Street address, planning roughly 1.4 million gross square feet across buildings up to four stories, and said that once operational the Omaha metro would hold the company's largest Google operational footprint of any US metro area, spanning this campus alongside the older Papillion site in neighboring Sarpy County and a newer Lincoln, Nebraska campus under construction on roughly 580 acres. Governor Pete Ricketts' administration said at the time it expected Google's Nebraska jobs to at least double with the new investment, covering technician, engineer, maintenance, and security roles at facilities that run 24 hours a day; Google separately pledged $100,000 toward Omaha's planned new main library. Since 2019 the company has created more than 120 jobs across its various Nebraska roles, and reports investing about $4.4 billion in the state cumulatively over the five years through 2024, including $930 million in 2024 alone. Google's own Nebraska data center location page does not identify which specific building on the northwest Omaha campus this OSM-mapped structure corresponds to, nor its individual square footage or MW capacity, so this registry records the 1.4-million-square-foot campus-wide figure as regional context rather than a fact specific to this building.

Omaha Public Power District, which serves the Douglas and Sarpy county campuses, has cited large-load data center demand from Google and other operators as a leading factor in its own long-range generation and transmission planning, and Nebraska's status as one of the few states where electricity is delivered entirely by public power districts rather than investor-owned utilities has repeatedly come up in coverage of why Google, Facebook, and other hyperscalers chose the Omaha-Lincoln corridor for a dense cluster of campuses.

reading.body:
Google operates a data center campus in Douglas County, Nebraska as part of a broader Omaha-area presence that also spans Sarpy County. Google announced this northwest Omaha facility in April 2022 but does not publish power capacity, square footage, or building-level specifications. No individual campus capacity is disclosed for any facility in Nebraska, making the actual size of this or any other state facility opaque to public analysis.

The facility sits in a regional corridor that includes Yahoo and Travelers operations across Douglas and Sarpy counties. Google's Papillion campus in Sarpy County, the eighth data center confirmed in that county, represents approximately $600 million in reported investment, suggesting similar scale or investment level may characterize the Douglas County site, though this is not confirmed. Nebraska's published data center capacity across all mapped facilities remains zero megawatts.

This campus cannot be ranked or compared by power capacity using published data. Across Nebraska's 21 mapped facilities, not one operator discloses individual site megawatts. Without disclosed specifications, the campus matters to AI scaling primarily as evidence of Google's continued expansion into the Omaha region, but its actual contribution to the grid constraint cannot be quantified from public sources.
